sys_power: apply suspend argument in post-programmed wakealarm There are two wakealarm stragies for power daemon client programs: One is using pre-programmed wakealarm to ensure the device responses in a deterministic time while the other is using post-programmed wakealarm for validation of firmware and platform integration. Given the CL:1517064 followed by CL:1629167 and CL:1680384, the argument of 'wakeup_timeout' changed (back) from a post-programmed wakealarm to pre-progrmmmed one; considering the autotest purpose here, we shall revise the suspend time argument to adapt the new post-programmed wakealarm of 'suspend_for_sec'. init: Fix firmware update splash screen hang This issue occurred when a device was booted from USB and a firmware update (fingerprint, keyboard, or touch), that requires a reboot, took place. When booted from USB, the reboot request should be ignore, the critical update splash screen should be removed, and the boot should be allowed to proceed. The error was that the boot splash screen was never removed. This issue was introduced with crrev.com/c/1589050 . This CL corrects the logic, such that this boot splash screen is removed when booting from USB. The login screen should be shown # on next boot. attestation: OpenSSL1.1-compatible way to parse RSA-OAEP for TPM1.2 OpenSSL1.1 doesn't allow to get public key string from the cert. However, OpenSSL doesn't support decoding the RSA-OAEP key type. The way to deal with this is to add the algorithm alias so RSA-OAEP key type is treated as an alias of RSA. 1. add the algorithm alias when initilaizing OpenSSL. 2. decode the public key into EVP_PKEY and then RSA, and then encode it. BUT=chromium:942487 BUG=b:141344933 TEST=unittest for TPM1.2, TPM2.0 TEST=attestation_client verify_attestation --ek-only Change-Id: If4d2965822086be79043d7dd670dfc8445a98fa8 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1834816 Tested-by: Leo Lai <cylai@google.com> Commit-Ready: Leo Lai <cylai@google.com> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Andrey Pronin <apronin@chromium.org>
